subject: Geo-fence sunset + retention-trigger language — DPA redline Q&A
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@finserve.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-01T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on backup retention & geo-sunset triggers for DPA redline

Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this through — quick list from our side as we review the DPA redline. We need to lock the deletion/retention language so our compliance team can sign off. Two items that are blocking for us: 

1) Backups and incremental snapshots: your current language says "backup copies may be retained for disaster recovery purposes." We need clarity on whether backups are considered part of the primary erase SLA (i.e., are they erased within the same window), or whether you consider backups exempt and provide a separate assurance (and proof) for wipe.

2) Geo-fence sunset: if an EU region is sunsetted (cloud provider region retired or we change residency to another zone), what triggers a migration vs. an onshore-wipe? We need precise triggers and timelines (e.g., notification, migration, forced wipe after X days), and evidence we can request.

3) Evidence type: for erasure we accept either (a) wipe certificates with timestamps and deleted object IDs, or (b) logs + snapshot manifest showing removal from durable storage. Please confirm what Redwood will provide.

4) Legal hold: how will you support a customer-initiated legal hold that needs to pause erasure for a subset of customer records? What's the process and expected timelines to surface that to the engineering/ops team?

Can you propose specific redline language we can agree on (short, precise) or propose options? We want to avoid vague phrasing that makes signoff slow.

Thanks,
Daniel
Data Protection Officer, FinServe

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <dpark@finserve.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-02T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on backup retention & geo-sunset triggers for DPA redline

Daniel — thanks, clear list. Internal team looped in for technical/legal detail. Attached is a working redline (FinServe_DPA_Redline_v1.docx) and our evidence matrix. High level proposals below; we'll iterate quickly.

Proposal A (default):
- Primary data erasure: Redwood will delete customer primary data and associated logical snapshots from production storage within 30 days after termination or verified deletion request.
- Backup copies: Necessary backups retained for disaster recovery will be retained up to 90 days after deletion request. Backup copies will be logically expired and deleted on the next scheduled backup cycle; Redwood will provide a timestamped affidavit of deletion and a manifest of deleted snapshot IDs.

Proposal B (tighter for regulated customers):
- Backup copies retained no longer than 30 days and Rolling-snapshot TTL enforced; where onshore backup copies exist, Redwood will schedule an onshore wipe and provide proof within 45 days.

Geo-fence sunset triggers (suggested language):
- If Redwood intends to decommission or change the region serving a FinServe tenant, Redwood will (i) notify FinServe at least 60 days in advance with a migration plan; (ii) provide an option to migrate data to an alternative region with equivalent residency; (iii) if FinServe elects not to migrate, Redwood will schedule an onshore wipe within 30 days of election, and provide erase evidence within 45 days.

Evidence: Redwood will provide either a wipe affidavit (signed) plus deleted snapshot manifest OR a signed export of deletion logs and object manifests identifying deleted keys/IDs. Evidence delivery: secure shared drive link or DocuSign.

Legal holds: FinServe can register a scoped legal hold via the Redwood Console (or support ticket). Upon registration Redwood will (i) suspend scheduled erasure for impacted records, (ii) notify the customer of any effect to recovery/retention timelines, and (iii) provide an acknowledgement within 48 hours. Restorative steps to resume erasure will be agreed by both parties.

Asking the team: Marissa, do those terms match our standard DPA playbook and evidence formats? Karthik/Ben — can you confirm operational feasibility and the expected backstop timelines (backup cycle window, manifest generation ETA)? I can then send a short redline back to Daniel and legal.

—Vanessa
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Daniel Park <dpark@finserve.com>

Date: 2028-10-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on backup retention & geo-sunset triggers for DPA redline

Vanessa / Daniel — quick privacy/compliance view. The proposals look good; a few clarifications and a recommended phrasing set that keeps contractual language testable: 

1) Use "primary production data" and "disaster recovery snapshots (backups)" as distinct terms. Contract text: "Primary production data" means data in active storage used to serve requests; "Disaster recovery snapshots" means point-in-time backup artifacts.

2) For backups we should offer two controlled options explicitly in contract: (i) "retention-cutoff: 30 days" or (ii) "retention-cutoff: 90 days with a backup-erasure-playbook delivered on request." Avoid vague "may be retained."

3) Evidence: We typically provide a signed "Erase Certificate" that includes (a) snapshot IDs, (b) wipe timestamps (UTC), and (c) method used (logical delete / cryptographic erasure). For backups stored in third-party vendor immutable stores, we provide export of immutability logs + vendor deletion confirmation. Suggested clause: "Customer may request Erase Certificate within 30 days after deletion and Redwood will provide within 15 business days."

4) Legal hold workflow: keep it simple operationally — require a ticket plus legal contact. Clause: "Upon receipt of a legal hold request referencing Customer ID and scoped data selectors, Redwood will pause automated erasure for that selector and confirm via ticket within 48 hours. Redwood will, upon Customer authorization, resume erasure or provide a mutually-agreed remedy."

I'll attach a short evidence template (redwood-erase-evidence-matrix.xlsx). Minor point: avoid hard "DocuSign only" for evidence delivery — allow secure drive + signed PDF or DocuSign.

-Marissa
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Questions on backup retention & geo-sunset triggers for DPA redline

Technical runbook/details from infra side: 

- Backup cadence & TTL: Our standard is incremental snapshots every 6 hours, full snapshot nightly. Snapshots are tagged with customer ID and TTL metadata. The earliest backup eviction window is the next full-snapshot cycle after retention cutoff. Practically, with a 30-day retention-cutoff, backups are removed within 30-36 days; with 90-day cutoff, within 90-96 days. We can contract to "within X days after the retention cutoff" to allow for scheduled cycles.

- Onshore copies: For customers with onshore backup copies, those are stored in a distinct bucket with scheduled purge jobs. We can commit to scheduling an explicit onshore wipe job and provide the job run manifest. Expectation: manifests available within 7 business days after the wipe job completes.

- Geo-sunset: two triggers: (a) Redwood-initiated provider region deprecation, or (b) explicit Customer instruction to change residency. For (a) we will give 60 days notice and offer migration. If customer declines, onshore wipe scheduled within 30 days after decline. For (b) we perform migration unless customer requests deletion; deletion path will follow retention-cutoff timelines above.

- Proof artifacts: we can provide (i) snapshot manifest (IDs + hash), (ii) object metadata deletion events, (iii) job execution logs (job ID, completion timestamp). Recommended contract language: "Evidence shall include job IDs and manifests sufficient to correlate deleted artifacts to the Customer tenant IDs."

Operational ask: Ben, can you confirm ops SLA to produce manifests within 7 business days? If yes, we can harden the clause to "evidence provided within 10 business days."

-Karthik
SVP, Infrastructure

Daniel / Hannah — thanks for patience. Based on the threads above, next steps we propose so legal can close the loop quickly: 

1) Contract language: we will send a concise redline that implements the following points: (a) "Primary production data" deleted within 30 days of termination or validated erase request; (b) "Disaster recovery snapshots" retention-cutoff option selectable by customer (30 or 90 days) with a default of 90 days; (c) explicit geo-sunset notification/migration option with 60 days notice and onshore wipe within 30 days if customer elects deletion.

2) Evidence delivery: Redwood to provide Erase Certificate or manifest within 10 business days of evidence request. Delivery via secure Drive share or DocuSign per customer preference.

3) Legal hold: ticket + legal contact required; Redwood to acknowledge within 48 hours and pause automated erasure for scoped selectors.

4) Ops commitments: Karthik confirmed snapshot eviction windows and a 7-business-day ETA for onshore wipe manifests; Ben will confirm internal ops booking for retest within 48 hours.

Attachments: FinServe_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (redline), redwood-erase-evidence-matrix.xlsx (evidence template).

If that works for FinServe we'll send a short redline and a DocuSign envelope for signature. Proposed timeline: redline sent by EOD Friday (2028-10-06), FinServe feedback within 5 business days, final signoff targeted by 2028-10-20.

Please let me know any missing items; happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow if you'd prefer.

Best,
